paper.title: Contextual Safety Reasoning and Grounding for Open-World Robots
paper.central_claim: CORE infers contextual constraints online without prebuilt maps/specifications, grounds them spatially and enforces them with probabilistic safety guarantees under perception uncertainty, approaching an oracle and outperforming non-contextual methods in unseen settings.

sections_read: Appendix B including tasks, uncertainty optimization and prompt

evidence.quote: The robot is provided with high-level safety guidelines
evidence.support_explanation: No environment-specific rules required but guidelines and operator semantics are supplied.

evidence.quote: The final output is a JSON object containing the VLM’s justification, safety-relevant semantics, and the predicates defining safe and unsafe regions,
updates to h(x) cannot instantaneously classify the robot’s current position as unsafe.
evidence.support_explanation: Safe initialization at map updates is essential, not automatic.

evidence.quote: We evaluate four tasks per environment—two safe and two unsafe—and we repeat each task five times, yielding 60 evaluations.
evidence.support_explanation: Complete simulation task denominator with repeats.

evidence.support_explanation: Counted physical transfer; per-task rates only pooled by type.

signatures.information: Streaming RGB, high-level guidelines, fixed ON/NEAR/AROUND/BETWEEN semantics; no prior map or local hazard rules.
signatures.operation: 4-bit Gemma3-27B infers semantic classes and safe/unsafe predicate JSON online.
signatures.conditions: Hazards detectable early; field of view; structured prompt.
signatures.feedback: New camera frames; no outcome-optimized self-modification.
signatures.selection_rule: Fixed structured inference, not candidate optimization
signatures.selection_data: Runtime observations; VLM choice uses100 images from setup.
signatures.persistence: Rules/map counts maintained during operation; model/prompt static.
signatures.later_use: Grounding module and subsequent control cycles.
signatures.failure_boundary: Missed wet-floor sign or late detection; no per-frame uncertainty estimates.

signatures.information: SAM3 masks, depth/odometry, thresholded safe-count grid, known dynamics; Spot depth scaled with measured returns.
signatures.operation: Project predicates into SDF barrier; solve minimum-change CBF QP; regulate traversal against calibrated detection function.
signatures.conditions: Control-affine dynamics; valid conservative detection model, safe radius; updates must not make current pose unsafe.
signatures.feedback: RGB-D/odometry at slower perception and faster control loops
signatures.selection_rule: QP feasibility and barrier inequality; certificate parameter search at fixed risk target
signatures.selection_data: Calibration on100 setup images; gamma=0 assumed in worked certificate
signatures.persistence: Within-run map only; no retained training/skill improvement claim.
signatures.claimed_effect: Probabilistic context safety with minimal deviation
signatures.failure_boundary: Grounding ghosts block safe motion; contextual distribution/temporal correlation and moving-state supermartingale condition not fully empirically validated.

gap.author_gap: User-specified semantic constraints cannot cover unknown contextual hazards; geometry-only filters miss social/semantic boundaries.
gap.checked_gap: Demonstrated gap between generic upfront safety rules and visually inferred constraints on prescribed unsafe tasks; strong physical-control integration, not unrestricted open-world safety.

lineage.version: as cited in v2; originals not supplied

gap.closest_adjacent: Prior semantics-to-costmap safety vs online VLM-generated constraints; perception-induced barrier uncertainty rather than only state error.
gap.residue: Ground contextual predicates in usable geometry and control risk under missed semantic detections.
gap.stakes: Collision-free paths can still violate semantic exclusion zones.
gap.method_response: Structured predicates→depth-grounded safe sets→QP filter with probabilistic analysis.
gap.remaining_gap: Dynamic contexts, calibration shift, timely detection and proof-to-discrete implementation assurance.
unresolved: No independent theorem verification or calibrated worst-context risk test.

condition_checks.condition: Reliable proxy for true contextual safety

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: VLM safety predicates become grounded metric constraints consumed by independent CBF solver.
pattern_mapping.necessary_conditions_and_differences: Checker only certifies safe set it receives; cannot certify missing semantics. Continuous projection differs from request rejection.

expectations.reason: No-context controlled comparison and one-at-a-time prompt removal; no grounding/QP/uncertainty closed-loop toggle.
Five randomized-start repeats per task and failure types; no task-level confidence interval/paired significance.
Context/grounding/enforcement split plus safe-vs-unsafe success; not just positive success.
Six tasks×5 specified; pooled class rates rather than all six per-task rates.
Sensor projection intrinsics, calibrated-depth scaling and failures/range limitations disclosed.
Same CBF for baselines; hardware and model/module latency reported, no complete run-token/energy budget.

claims.text: Online contextual safety approaches oracle and outperforms fixed rules.
claims.setting: Three IsaacSim scenes,12 tasks×5 random starts
claims.baseline/control: Oracle98.3%, no-context55%, geometry50%, common CBF synthesis
claims.selection_vs_test: Safety scenarios explicitly designed; model selected on100 images from same setup; no independent held-out development protocol
counterevidence: Setup-specific scenario construction and model-selection images; not uncontrolled open-world distribution.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Reported controlled-scene advantage of online context.

claims.text: Safety framework transfers to real Spot.
claims.selection_vs_test: Lab transfer; depth implementation adjusted for hardware
counterevidence: Only single lab; full per-task rates not tabulated.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Counted sim-to-real execution, not broad open-world guarantee.

claims.text: Probabilistic bounds guarantee90% safe trajectories and empirically validate safety.
claims.setting: Conservative distance detection function and safe initial radius; derived CBF/NSM certificate
claims.selection_vs_test: Certificate calibration and simulation setup overlap; no independent risk-calibration test
claims.result/denominator: Main text gamma=one-third risk; worked appendix certificate gamma=0 with explicitly non-conservative context-independent assumption
counterevidence: Conditional-supermartingale requirement is stronger than unconditional expectation bound; not established for arbitrary moving/context-changing robot by fixed-position monotonicity.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Conditional theoretical certificate and descriptive safety rates; no independently established universal open-world probability bound.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Author reports substantial contextual safety gains in repeated simulated tasks and26/30 real Spot trials. Guarantees depend on safe initialization, conservative/context-stable detection calibration and conditional process assumptions; general open-world risk is not validated.
